grades.quote: The most important characterization of a given memory address range is whether it holds regular main memory or I/O devices.
grades.reason: RISC-V passage says the key PMA characterization of an address range is regular main memory versus I/O devices. This is the device-versus-memory distinction, but it doesn't explicitly tie it to cacheability.

grades.quote: If a PMA indicates non-cacheability, then accesses to that region must be satisfied by the memory itself, not by any caches.
grades.reason: RISC-V passage on cacheability PMAs. It says cacheability is a platform-level PMA setting and that non-cacheable accesses must be satisfied by the memory itself. It also mentions the main memory versus I/O classification as a separate PMA. It is useful but doesn't fully spell out how cacheable and device accesses are distinguished.
